prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” broker for everyone — the right broker depends on your needs (individual vs family vs Medicare vs small‑business), whether you want in‑person help, whether you need an independent agent who can show plans from many carriers, and other preferences (languages, evening availability, fees, etc.). I can help you find a great broker in Kansas City if you tell me more about what you need. Meanwhile, here’s a practical way to find the best fit and some concrete next steps.

How to find a good Kansas City health insurance broker
- Decide what kind of plan you need: individual/family (ACA Marketplace), Medicare (Part A/B/D/Medigap/Advantage), Medicaid/CHIP, or employer group/SMB plans. Brokers often specialize.
- Prefer independent brokers/agents who represent multiple carriers (more options) rather than captive agents who sell only one carrier.
- Check credentials and licensing: verify the agent is licensed in Missouri or Kansas through the state insurance department (Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance; Kansas Insurance Department).
- Look at reviews and referrals: Google, Yelp, Facebook, and local community groups. Ask friends/co‑workers who had similar needs.
- Ask the right questions before committing (see the checklist below).

Useful resources
- NAHU “Find an Agent” tool (National Association of Health Underwriters) — helps locate credentialed brokers.
- healthcare.gov (for ACA Marketplace enrollment help and certified navigators/agents).
- Medicare.gov (for searching Medicare agents and counseling through SHIP — State Health Insurance Assistance Program).
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance or Kansas Insurance Department (to verify licensing and complaints).

Questions to ask a prospective broker
- Do you specialize in individual, small‑group, or Medicare plans?
- Are you independent (represent multiple carriers) or captive to one insurer?
- How long have you been helping clients with plans like mine?
- How do you get paid? (Most consumer brokers are paid by carriers, but ask if there are any fees.)
- Will you help with claims or problems after I enroll?
- Can you provide references or client reviews?
- Do you assist with tax credits/subsidies if I qualify (ACA marketplace)?
- Do you offer in‑person appointments and are you available during enrollment periods or emergencies?

Practical next steps I can do for you
- If you tell me your ZIP code and what type of coverage you need (individual/family, Medicare, employer plan help), I can look up several well‑rated local brokers/agents, summarize their specialties, and give contact details.
- Or I can walk you step‑by‑step through comparing plans if you give me your approximate income, ages covered, and any preferred doctors or medications.

Tell me: ZIP code and what kind of plan you’re shopping for, and I’ll find a few good local brokers and give tailored questions to ask them.
